```text
# #2923: Patch: a finished game counts once in your statistics, even after you watch its replay
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When an online or practice game ends, pressing Watch replay (or Share last turn) and then Back counts that game a second time in your statistics. You get one more win or loss, a longer streak, and the cards on the final board counted as seen again. Every trip through the replay adds another copy. The inflated totals are then sent to your account, so your public player summary is wrong too.

Once this is built, a game counts once however often you open its replay.

## Why

- `useGameStats` (`apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.ts:15-43`) keeps its already-recorded flag in a `useRef` (line 18). It records whenever a finished view arrives while the flag is false (lines 38-41), then calls `syncPlayerStats()`. That call PUTs the device's totals to `/api/stats/player` (`stats/sync.ts`).
- The ref only lasts as long as `Game` stays mounted, and both routes unmount `Game` to show the replay:
  - the online route returns `<OpenedReplay>` instead of the board while `watching !== null && view.result !== null` (`apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx:392`);
  - practice returns `<ReplayPlayer>` for its finished game (`apps/web/src/routes/practice.tsx:1186-1200`).
- Back clears `watching`, so `Game` mounts again on the finished view. The hook's first run sees an outcome with the flag false and records the game again.
- Nothing catches the repeat. `recordGame` (`stats/store.ts:106`) and `addGame` (`stats/model.ts`) do no de-duplication, and the hook has no test (there is no `useGameStats.test.ts`).

## Proposal

Record only a game whose unfinished view this mount has seen. The record condition becomes `outcome !== null && !recorded.current && before !== null && outcomeOfView(before) === null`. A game that is already over in the first view of a mount (a remount after a replay, a reload on the result screen) has either been counted already or has an empty log. The rest of the hook stays as it is.

## Where it lands

- `apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.ts`.
- A new `apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.test.ts`.
- SPEC §9.11 and R639 are unchanged: this only makes R639's once-per-game hold. No new ruling.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Rendering the hook with a live view and then the finished one gives `games` 1.
- [ ] Unmounting and rendering the hook again with the same finished view leaves `games` at 1 and makes no second sync call. This fails today.
- [ ] A new game after a finished one on the same mount still counts: live, finished, live, finished gives 2.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/stats` passes.

## Size and risks

Small: a few lines and one test file. One case stops counting on the device: a game the player was away from when it ended, then reopened already finished. Today that case counts with an empty log. The server's own records of online games are unaffected.

4. This guards the reset path (lines 26-32) against the new condition. The existing "a new game on the same board starts a log of its own" test already covers the live → finished → live → finished-draw shape, so keep it passing unmodified.
5. Run `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/stats/useGameStats.test.tsx` (rebuilds the WASM module first), then `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/stats`, plus `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `pnpm --dir apps/web exec eslint apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.ts apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.test.tsx` if eslint covers the web app per CLAUDE.md.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.test.tsx`, `it("R639 a remount on the finished view counts nothing and syncs nothing")`: live → finished gives `games` 1 and one `syncPlayerStats` call; a fresh mount on the same finished view leaves `games` at 1 with no second sync call. Fails before the fix (games becomes 2, sync called twice).
- `apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.test.tsx`, `it("R639 live, finished, live, finished on one mount counts two")`: two full games on one mount give `games` 2. Passes before and after; guards the reset path.
- Existing five tests in the same file stay green unmodified, in particular "logs a finished game once" and "a new game on the same board starts a log of its own".
- Commands: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/stats/useGameStats.test.tsx`, then `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/stats`.

## Done when

- [ ] Live → finished on one mount records exactly one game.
- [ ] A fresh mount on the same finished view records nothing and makes no second `syncPlayerStats` call.
- [ ] Live, finished, live, finished on one mount records two games.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/stats` passes; typecheck and eslint on the touched files pass.
- [ ] No spec, ruling, route, `Game.tsx`, or stats-helper file changed.

## Risks

- One known behavior change, stated in the issue: a game the player was away from when it ended, then opened already finished (first view of the mount is over), no longer counts on the device and its log is empty. Accepted: it matches the proposal, and the server's own records of online games are unaffected.
- The `previous.current === view` early return (line 21) means rerendering the identical view object is a no-op; the remount test must use a new `renderHook` (fresh refs), not a rerender, to reproduce the bug.
- React StrictMode double-invokes the effect in dev, but the hook has no cleanup and the second run sees `previous.current === view` and returns early, so the new condition is evaluated once per distinct view; no extra guard needed.

## Open questions

None.

## State

Plan reviewed; code and spec sections re-read. `outcomeOfView` is already imported in `useGameStats.ts`. Doing failing-test-first: add the two R639 tests (remount + two-games) with a `syncPlayerStats` spy, run to see the remount one fail, then apply the one-line condition fix, then run the stats suite + typecheck + eslint.

## Log

- 2026-11-03: starting; adding the two regression tests first to observe the remount failure before the fix.
- 2026-11-03: remount test fails as predicted (games 2 after remount); two-games guard passes pre-fix. Fix applied to the record condition; now verifying.
- 2026-11-03: done. `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/stats` green (14 files, 255 tests), typecheck clean, eslint clean on both files. Only the two intended files changed.

## Goal

Stop a finished online or practice game from counting twice in the device's player statistics when the player opens its replay (or Share last turn) and comes back: `Game` unmounts for the replay and remounts on the finished view, and the remount's first hook run must not record. Once built, a game counts once however often its replay is opened; SPEC §9.11 and R639 are unchanged (this only makes R639's once-per-game hold, so no new ruling).

## Files to touch

| File | New / change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.ts` | change | The record condition (line 38): also require a seen unfinished view this mount |
| `apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.test.tsx` | change | Extend the existing `describe("R639 useGameStats")` with remount and sync-call tests |

Note: the issue asks for "a new `apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.test.ts`", but that file already exists as `apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.test.tsx` (101 lines, five `R639` tests); extend it, do not create a second file.

Must not touch: anything under `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/` or `bot/`; `spec/` (no new ruling); `crates/*`; the routes (`apps/web/src/routes/match.tsx`, `apps/web/src/routes/practice.tsx`), `apps/web/src/game/Game.tsx`, or the stats helpers (`model.ts`, `store.ts`, `sync.ts`, `track.ts`). Governing spec: §9.11 and R639 (`spec/rulings/R0639.md`).

## Steps

1. In `apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.ts`, change only the record condition (line 38) from `if (outcome !== null && !recorded.current)` to `if (outcome !== null && !recorded.current && before !== null && outcomeOfView(before) === null)`. `before` is the `previous.current` captured on line 22 before the assignment on line 23, and `outcomeOfView` is already imported (line 13), so no new import. Add a two-line comment above it, in the file's existing style, e.g. that a mount whose first view is already over (a remount after a replay, a reload on the result screen) records nothing because it either counted already or has an empty log.
2. In `apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.test.tsx`, reuse the file's existing helpers (`viewWith`, `play`, `baseView`, `emptySide`, `card`) unchanged. Add `import * as syncModule from "./sync.ts"` plus `vi` from `vitest` and `afterEach` if not imported; in `beforeEach` start `vi.spyOn(syncModule, "syncPlayerStats")` (wrapping the real implementation, which is a silent no-op with no session token) and in `afterEach` call `vi.restoreAllMocks()`. Copy this spy pattern from `apps/web/src/stats/sync.test.ts` lines 16-19 only for style; the spy approach keeps the existing five tests' behavior identical.
3. Add test `it("R639 a remount on the finished view counts nothing and syncs nothing", ...)`: render the hook with a live view, rerender with the finished view (same `viewWith` + `{ result: { winner: "p1", reason: "hero-death" } }` pattern as the first existing test), assert `readPlayerStats().games` is 1 and the sync spy has been called once; then `unmount()`, `renderHook` again with the same finished view object, and assert `games` is still 1 and the spy is still at one call. This is the test that fails today.
4. Add test `it("R639 live, finished, live, finished on one mount counts two", ...)`: on a single mount, rerender live → finished (win) → live (`baseView` with no result) → finished (win with a different winner or reason), and assert `games` is 2. This guards the reset path (lines 26-32) against the new condition. The existing "a new game on the same board starts a log of its own" test already covers the live → finished → live → finished-draw shape, so keep it passing unmodified.
5. Run `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/stats/useGameStats.test.tsx` (rebuilds the WASM module first), then `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/stats`, plus `pnpm --dir apps/web typecheck` and `pnpm --dir apps/web exec eslint apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.ts apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.test.tsx` if eslint covers the web app per CLAUDE.md.

## Tests

- `apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.test.tsx`, `it("R639 a remount on the finished view counts nothing and syncs nothing")`: live → finished gives `games` 1 and one `syncPlayerStats` call; a fresh mount on the same finished view leaves `games` at 1 with no second sync call. Fails before the fix (games becomes 2, sync called twice).
- `apps/web/src/stats/useGameStats.test.tsx`, `it("R639 live, finished, live, finished on one mount counts two")`: two full games on one mount give `games` 2. Passes before and after; guards the reset path.
- Existing five tests in the same file stay green unmodified, in particular "logs a finished game once" and "a new game on the same board starts a log of its own".
- Commands: `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/stats/useGameStats.test.tsx`, then `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/stats`.

## Done when

- [ ] Live → finished on one mount records exactly one game.
- [ ] A fresh mount on the same finished view records nothing and makes no second `syncPlayerStats` call.
- [ ] Live, finished, live, finished on one mount records two games.
- [ ] `pnpm --dir apps/web test src/stats` passes; typecheck and eslint on the touched files pass.
- [ ] No spec, ruling, route, `Game.tsx`, or stats-helper file changed.

## Risks

- One known behavior change, stated in the issue: a game the player was away from when it ended, then opened already finished (first view of the mount is over), no longer counts on the device and its log is empty. Accepted: it matches the proposal, and the server's own records of online games are unaffected.

- React StrictMode double-invokes the effect in dev, but the hook has no cleanup and the second run sees `previous.current === view` and returns early, so the new condition is evaluated once per distinct view; no extra guard needed.

## Open questions

None.
